candidates.snippet:
## Problem Statement

业务用户用自然语言说出的问题，要落成禅道里的单据。现在这条链路是自研拼装：写入靠随包脚本换令牌、绕开自研禅道 MCP 的固定身份（#7/#12），图片靠脚本直连禅道 REST v2（#8），列表靠查询器在进程内做字段投影（#10）。这套拼装留下四个未修的服务端 issue、三支自研脚本和多个 ADR。

禅道官方已经出了 `zentao-cli`（MIT，npm 包）。可行性验证结论：它在我们这台 max 8.2 实例上覆盖了技能需要的全部能力（#13）。迁过去以后，凭据仍只在业务用户本机，令牌每次现换、经环境变量注入 CLI，不进 argv、不进 Agent 上下文、不落盘；单据留痕在当前账号名下。

顺带一个与换不换 CLI 无关的既存缺陷：反馈单的「反馈者」字段在这台实例上不会被禅道自动记录，技能却拿它核对提交人，给业务用户的结论是错的（#14）。

## Solution

技能改用官方禅道 CLI 作为唯一接入通道：读、写、传图都走 `zentao` 命令；随包脚本收缩成一个入口脚本（换令牌、注入、落载荷、回读校验）和一个查重助手（中文关键词变体）。首次接入多一步「装 CLI」，少一步「登记禅道 MCP」。反馈单的提交人核对改看 `openedBy`，反馈者字段显式填当前禅道账号。

## User Stories

1. 作为

candidates.title: fix(subtitle): split Thai and Lao scripts at the spaces between sentences
candidates.snippet: Thai and Lao text separates sentences with a space instead of a full stop. `split_string_by_punctuations()` ends a script line only at `PUNCTUATIONS` and at line breaks, so a Thai or Lao paragraph is one script line. With an Edge TTS voice and the default `subtitle_provider = "edge"`, the video then shows the whole narration as one subtitle: a 6-sentence script stands on screen as a 6-line block for all of its 16 seconds, and a longer one runs off the top of the frame. Thai is one of the 14 script languages in the WebUI (`th-TH` in `support_locales`), the voice list has `th-TH-PremwadeeNeural`
candidates.problem: Thai and Lao subtitles are not split into separate lines because the scripts use spaces instead of punctuation, causing long, unreadable subtitle blocks in TTS videos.
candidates.selfBuiltSolution: Modified the subtitle splitting function (split_string_by_punctuations) to also split Thai and Lao scripts at spaces between sentences, ensuring each sentence appears as its own subtitle line.
candidates.reasoning: The author identifies a specific multilingual subtitle issue and implements a concrete code fix, demonstrating a lead‑user need and self‑built solution.

candidates.author: everforward
candidates.title: You can do the "almost-realtime" part, all locally.
candidates.snippet: You can do the "almost-realtime" part, all locally. I tinkered with a Python script for a few hours that used Whisper to speech-to-text, fed that into a local Mistral model (don't recall which), and then piped the output into text-to-speech. It wasn't really streamed, though. Audio input was buffered, fully evaluated to a string, then fed into the LLM and the full text was converted back to audio. The Whisper speech-to-text was pretty real-time, the LLM was not. I was barely scraping by on hardware specs, though.
candidates.problem: Need for near real-time, fully local speech-to-speech conversion using AI models
candidates.selfBuiltSolution: Created a Python script that buffers audio, runs Whisper for speech-to-text, feeds the transcript into a local Mistral LLM, then pipes the generated text into a text-to-speech engine
